title: Brass bands at funerals and the music coming back
summary: Bands played for society parades and for deceased band members, with slow pieces going and lively ones coming back along the levee.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, I guess you remember when the Pickwick band played funerals then? Oh, yeah.

Well, I used to play in the brass band myself, lately, you know. I mean, after we had the string band, we used to play all the parades they had. Every society would have a banquet, they would have a brass band to play, to play the parade, and every member of the band that would die would play the parade, you know, for the funeral.

Yeah. Any member of any band around the community would die, the band would parade. All the band would get together and play the parade. I mean, play the march, you know. And I told them I didn't want them to play for me, because coming back they played all kind of fast, I don't even like that.
Do they still play the halls up here?
No, they don't. The last one we played was for a man, I forgot to mention his name, he played with me, too. He played bass, Ersk and Tony. He played for his funeral. Ersk and Tony? Uh-huh.
About how long ago was that?

That's been about, what, between eight and ten years? Yeah. Well, what kind of music would the brass bands play? Well, they played mostly Detroit pieces, you know, going to the funeral. But coming back there, they played on Glad You're Dead, Ersk, Ersk, Ersk, Ersk, Ersk, all pieces like that, you know. And just bust it out on the personal levee, coming back from the funeral. I didn't like that idea. On the levee they play?
Most of the time, you know, people, they used to play, they walk on the levee, they didn't pass in the low, they, you know, it was cool on the levee, I guess.
Yeah. Well, did they used to play funnels when you were growing up? Oh, yeah, sure. Did they play that kind of writing music?
Coming back, sure, they always did.
Even when you were a little boy. Yeah.
